# GitHub Copilot custom models (BYOK): Microsoft Foundry runbook

GitHub documents enterprise and organization custom models as a settings form;
no REST API or configuration file for it is documented. This runbook is the
desired state for that form, derived from the deployment inventory. The same
data is in `custom-models.json` for audits and drift reviews.

Models registered here appear in the model picker for **Copilot Chat, Copilot
CLI and IDEs**. GitHub Agentic Workflows are a separate path: gh-aw documents
BYOK only as per-workflow `engine.env` settings, and nothing in its reference
says it consults this registry. Configure those from each deployment's
`gh-aw/` folder.

## Where to enter it

- **Enterprise:** Enterprise → **AI controls** → **Copilot** → **Configure custom models** → **Add API key**
- **Organization:** Organization settings → **Copilot** → **Models** → **Custom models** tab → **Add API key**

GitHub allows **one Deployment URL per API key entry**. Deployments that share
a URL are grouped below as multiple Model IDs under one entry.

## Key entries

### 1. `foundry-dev-fdy-myass-dev-eus2`

| Form field | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider | Microsoft Foundry |
| Name | `foundry-dev-fdy-myass-dev-eus2` |
| API key | value of secret `FOUNDRY_DEV_API_KEY` (resource key for `fdy-myass-dev-eus2`, dev) |
| Deployment URL | `https://fdy-myass-dev-eus2.openai.azure.com/openai/v1` |
| Model IDs (add each) | `gpt-41-dev`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-oss-120b` |

If the form rejects the Deployment URL, try these in order and then set
`enterprise_url_style` in the inventory so the runbook matches what worked:

- `https://fdy-myass-dev-eus2.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-41-dev/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21`
- `https://fdy-myass-dev-eus2.openai.azure.com`

A per-deployment URL serves one model only. If that is the form that works,
this entry splits into 3 entries, one per Model ID; setting
`enterprise_url_style` to `deployment` regenerates the runbook that way.

## After saving

1. On the **Added models** tab, open **Configure** for each model, set it to
   **Enabled**, then use the **Access** tab to choose **Allow for all
   organizations** or **Choose per organization**.
2. Confirm the model appears at the bottom of the Copilot Chat model picker
   under the enterprise (or organization) name.
3. Send one prompt, then check the Azure resource's metrics for a matching
   request on the expected deployment.

## Notes

- **Model ID is the Azure deployment name.** On Azure the `model` field of a
  request carries the deployment name, so that is what the form needs.
- **Least privilege.** Use a key for a resource that hosts only the
  deployments you intend to expose; an Azure resource key grants every
  deployment on that resource.
- **Key-based auth must be enabled** on the Azure resource
  (`disableLocalAuth=false`). The form cannot use Entra ID.
- **Rotation.** After regenerating a key in Azure, edit the key entry here and
  update the matching GitHub Actions secret in the same change window.
- The feature is in public preview; field names and navigation can change.
